newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics surprises with revenue.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics surprises with revenue.

text.p: Modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp pleasantly surprised the market on Monday, reporting revenue and earnings in line with expectations for its fiscal 1996 fourth quarter, analysts said.

"Overall they managed to pull the rabbit out of the hat, at least for the quarter," said Rakesh Sood, an analyst for Hambrecht & Quist. "People were pretty bearish all the way around and were thinking they wouldn't hit their numbers."

After reporting third-quarter revenues had grown 20 percent versus the second quarter of fiscal 1996, the company cautioned that sequential growth in the fourth quarter would not be as strong. It had projected average second-half growth of 15 percent versus the second quarter, meaning an increase of about 10 percent for the fourth quarter, analysts said.
But in fact, fourth-quarter revenue increased 11.8 percent over $546.8 million in the third quarter.

In fact, earnings matched the First Call consensus estimate of $0.71 a share, before acquisition charges, versus an adjusted $0.37 per share last year. Revenue of $611.4 million topped most estimates, which ranged from $600 million to $610 million. U.S. Robotics posted fourth-quarter revenue of $293.4 million the previous year.
"It was a great quarter -- in line with expectations is the best way to describe it," said Volpe, Welty & Co analyst Amar Senan.
In after-hours trade, shares of U.S. Robotics moved as high as 61, up 1-1/2 from the market close of 59-1/2.

In addition, U.S. Robotics said its gross margin in the fourth quarter held steady at 41.9 percent compared with the fiscal third quarter. The desktop modem market has been hit with stiff pricing competition, but the company said systems products posted higher sales as a percentage of total revenue, offsetting the reduced prices of modems.
"People thought something was going to have give, but they managed to deliver on all key metrics," Sood said.
